title: The 2026 State of Web Gaming: Developer & Player Study

observations.statement: The report is based on two Poki-commissioned online surveys conducted by Atomik Research, one of which covered 400 game developers in the US and UK.
observations.excerpt: This report is based on two online surveys commissioned by Poki and conducted by the MRS-certified creative market research agency Atomik Research. One set of questions were put to 400 game developers in the US and UK

observations.statement: Poki reports more than 100 million monthly active players in 2026, up from 10 million in 2020.
observations.excerpt: Poki itself sees more than 100 million monthly active players in 2026, up from 10 million in 2020.

observations.statement: 37% of surveyed gamers play web games multiple times per day.
observations.excerpt: 37% of gamers play web games ‘multiple times per day’

observations.statement: 46% of surveyed web gamers stopped playing a mobile game because it took too long to load, and 28% because the download was too large.
observations.excerpt: 46% of the web gamers surveyed for this report have stopped playing a mobile game because it took too long to open or load. 28%, meanwhile, have stopped playing a mobile gaming app because the download size was too large.

observations.statement: 62% of surveyed players have downloaded or purchased a game after discovering it on web.
observations.excerpt: 62% of players have downloaded or purchased a game after discovering a game on web

observations.statement: 36% of surveyed developers cite insufficient revenue as the biggest barrier to embracing web gaming.
observations.excerpt: 36% cite insufficient revenue as the biggest barrier to embracing web gaming

observations.statement: 53% of surveyed developers plan to port mobile games to browser in the next 12 months.
observations.excerpt: 53% plan to port mobile games to browser in the next 12 months
